official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 standing-advice currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency flood planning guidance was updated 28 May 2026 and requires a sustainable drainage strategy where development could affect drainage or lies in relevant flood-risk areas.

official_measurement_examples.name: National standards legal status
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2025 national SuDS standards are non-statutory design, maintenance and operation standards; they do not themselves grant planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Major-development maintenance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Major-development SuDS require suitable operational standards and maintenance arrangements for the lifetime of the development.

official_measurement_examples.name: Strategy and FRA separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A SuDS strategy can be a standalone document or part of a flood risk assessment, but submission is not the same as approval or verified drainage performance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local guidance preserved
official_measurement_examples.fact: Local plan, LLFA, LFRMS, SFRA and local SuDS guidance can add requirements and must not be replaced by a national-only assumption.

official_measurement_examples.name: Adoption separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Designing drainage to an adoption standard does not prove a sewerage undertaker has adopted it or that planning conditions are discharged.

official_measurement_examples.name: SWIM limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The May 2026 SWIM approach supports investment business cases for multiple SuDS features and is not a site-specific planning consent or drainage-capacity certificate.

official_measurement_examples.name: Capacity separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Flood and surface-water mapping identifies risk context and does not prove sewer, outfall or infiltration capacity for a parcel.

core_rules: SuDS standards are not planning permission
a drainage strategy is not an approved drainage solution
FRA submission is not condition discharge
national standards do not replace local LLFA requirements
surface-water risk mapping is not drainage-capacity evidence
sewer adoption must not be assumed from design intent
planning permission does not prove Building Regulations Part H compliance
SuDS compliance does not determine land ownership
SWIM funding appraisal is not parcel consent
historic drainage guidance retains version date
phased development requires phase-specific drainage performance
no parcel drainage clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, Defra, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. The 28 May 2026 flood-planning update and 2025 national SuDS standards were retained with planning, adoption, maintenance and capacity separation; no parcel promotion.
